tour.name: Phillip Island Private Tour from Melbourne: the Penguin Parade, Koalas & Wildlife
tour.subtitle: An afternoon and evening on Phillip Island with a local guide and car: kangaroos and wombats at a wildlife park, koalas on treetop boardwalks, the Nobbies and their fur seals, and at sunset the little penguins waddling ashore at the Penguin Parade.

tour.overview:
Every evening at sunset on Phillip Island, south-east of Melbourne, little penguins, the smallest penguins in the world at about 33 centimetres tall, return from a day of fishing at sea and waddle up the beach to their burrows in the dunes. The Penguin Parade, watched from grandstands and boardwalks, is one of Australia's most popular wildlife experiences, and the island's nature parks protect the colony of some 30,000 to 40,000 penguins.

This private afternoon and evening takes you there with a local guide and a car, with koalas, kangaroos and the coast along the way and premium viewing for the parade.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours (afternoon and evening)
• Start and end: your hotel in Melbourne
• Type: private tour with local guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• A wildlife park.
• The Koala Conservation Reserve.
• The Nobbies.
• The Penguin Parade.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private car avoids the long coach queues after the parade and lets you choose your stops.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, wildlife lovers and couples.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For a full day of coast, choose our Great Ocean Road tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Photography of the penguins is not allowed, to protect them. Evenings are cold and windy on the beach even in summer.

days.name: Kangaroos, koalas, the Nobbies and the Penguin Parade at sunset
days.description:
What to expect: Phillip Island's wildlife, with a local guide, private car and premium penguin viewing.

Your guide and driver collect you in the early afternoon and drive about two hours south-east to Phillip Island. On the way, you stop at a wildlife park to hand-feed kangaroos and see wombats, emus and Tasmanian devils.

On the island you walk the treetop boardwalks of the Koala Conservation Reserve, at eye level with koalas sleeping in the eucalyptus. At the Nobbies, a boardwalk follows the cliffs above the blowhole, with views of Seal Rocks, home to Australia's largest colony of fur seals.

At sunset, you take your premium seats at the Penguin Parade. As darkness falls, groups of little penguins appear in the surf and waddle up the beach and along the paths beside you to their burrows, calling to their chicks. After the parade, you drive back to Melbourne, arriving at about 22:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
13:00 – Pick-up in Melbourne.
14:30 – Wildlife park.
16:00 – Koala Conservation Reserve.
17:00 – The Nobbies.
18:00 – Dinner break (optional).
Sunset – Penguin Parade.
22:30 – Back in Melbourne.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The pick-up time follows sunset: from about 11:00 in winter to 15:00 in summer.
• Underground viewing or a guided ranger tour can be booked.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, local guide, entrance tickets, premium penguin viewing, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: none.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we photograph the penguins?
faq.answer: No. Photography is banned at the Penguin Parade to protect the penguins’ eyes and behaviour.

faq.question: How many penguins will we see?
faq.answer: Usually hundreds, sometimes over a thousand; numbers vary with the season.

faq.question: What is premium viewing?
faq.answer: Smaller viewing areas closer to the penguins’ path, with a ranger commentary.

faq.question: Is dinner included?
faq.answer: No. Your guide suggests a restaurant in Cowes before the parade.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, it is a family favourite. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Yes. The Penguin Parade has accessible viewing.

faq.question: Can we hold a koala?
faq.answer: Not in Victoria, but you see them close up on the boardwalks.

faq.question: How cold is it?
faq.answer: Cold and windy on the beach after dark, even in summer: bring warm layers.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Warm layers, a windproof jacket and comfortable shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Penguin numbers are highest in summer, from November to February.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not expected in Australia, where wages are higher, but it is always appreciated for excellent service.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
